newsitem.title: SPAIN: Repsol share offer details from prospectus.
newsitem.headline: Repsol share offer details from prospectus.

text.p: The final privatisation of Spain's Repsol, for which provisional orders can be made starting Monday, will allocate over half of the shares to small private investors and employees, according to the share prospectus presented to the stock market commission, CNMV.

In the privatisation of the state's last 10.0 percent stake of the energy firm, bidders will be given a rough estimate of how many shares they will eventually receive, in order to allow them to decide whether to maintain their offer.
The period for provisional share purchases ends on April 21.
The main details of the offer are as follow (all figures correspond to number of shares):
DOMESTIC TRANCHE: 14,791,409
Employees: 4,500,429
Institutions: 2,040,197
INTERNATIONAL TRANCHE: 8,160,778
Green shoe: 2,550,243
PRIVATISATION CALENDAR:
April 7-21: Provisional share orders can be made
April 21: Maximum sale price fixed
April 22: Underwriters of offer sign contract
April 22-24: Irrevocable share orders
April 28: Sale price fixed
Share orders made from today to April 21 will be given priority in the pro-rata allocation of shares.

The maximum sale price cannot exceed the highest of the average share price on the five consecutive sessions prior to the price fixing, up to and including the day on which the price is fixed (April 21).
Apart from the maximum share price, on April 22 an estimate will also be given of how many shares are likely to be allocated to each bidder.
The sale price for the retail tranche will be the lowest of three: the high during the sale period, the institutional price and the average traded price on April 28 with a discount of four percent.
The cost of the share offer will be around four billion pesetas.
The prospectus also sets out a pro-rata system on the basis of three norms:
- 50 percent of the retail tranche will be divided equally amongst all bidders - 35 percent of the retail tranche will be divided proportionally between the bids, up to 200 shares.
- the remaining 15 percent will be allocated proportionally amongst those bids which were not satisfied by the above two steps.
